# Herdr compatibility

<!-- Generated by tools/render_compatibility.py. Edit the gates it reads, not this file. -->

Which Herdr releases Tether 0.7.2 was exercised against, so it can be checked
before installing rather than inferred from a version requirement.

## Exercised

| Platform | Herdr release | How it was exercised |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ubuntu 24.04 | 0.8.0 | Official release asset, verified by SHA-256, then the live product smoke |
| macOS 14 | 0.8.0 | Official release asset, verified by SHA-256, then the live product smoke |

Every row is a real run: the gate downloads the official Herdr release asset for
the runner's platform, verifies it against a pinned SHA-256, validates the
socket API schema it reports, builds Tether from the locked manifest, and drives
a workload through `tmux` end to end. A row exists only for a platform that gate
actually covers.

## Socket protocol

Tether speaks Herdr's socket API from protocol 19, which Herdr 0.8.0 ships, and
its checks cover through protocol 20. A Herdr reporting a protocol above 20 is
not refused: `herdr-tether doctor` reports it as newer and not yet verified, and
Tether keeps working with the parts of the API it knows. A Herdr below protocol
19 is refused, because the requests Tether depends on are absent.

## What this does not claim

Herdr releases other than 0.8.0 are not covered here. Tether may work with them,
and its protocol floor is the real compatibility boundary at runtime, but this
table says only what was exercised.

Unreleased upstream Herdr is exercised separately, on a schedule, against
whatever `master` resolves to at the time. That canary is advisory: it catches
breakage early, and a moving revision is not something a user can install, so it
is deliberately absent from this table. Its behaviour reaches this document only
once it ships in a Herdr release the stable gate pins.
